claim: The duplication and ninefold symmetry of the Drosophila centriole requires that the cartwheel molecule, Sas6, physically associates with Gorab, a trans-Golgi component.
source: The duplication and ninefold symmetry of the Drosophila centriole requires that the cartwheel molecule, Sas6, physically associates with Gorab, a trans-Golgi component.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a key finding of the study, supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: A core stabilization sequence within Gorab's C-terminal coiled-coil domain enables homodimerization.
source: We identify a core stabilization sequence within Gorab's C-terminal coiled-coil domain that enables homodimerization, binding to Rab6, and thereby trans-Golgi localization.
evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data showing protected regions in the C-terminal domain and SEC-MALS data showing dimeric molecular weight.

claim: A core stabilization sequence within Gorab's C-terminal coiled-coil domain enables binding to Rab6.
source: We identify a core stabilization sequence within Gorab's C-terminal coiled-coil domain that enables homodimerization, binding to Rab6, and thereby trans-Golgi localization.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assays and HDX-MS data showing interaction between Gorab and Rab6.

claim: A core stabilization sequence within Gorab's C-terminal coiled-coil domain enables trans-Golgi localization.
source: We identify a core stabilization sequence within Gorab's C-terminal coiled-coil domain that enables homodimerization, binding to Rab6, and thereby trans-Golgi localization.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data showing Gorab localization at the trans-Golgi and loss of this localization when the dimerization core is deleted.

claim: Part of the Gorab monomer's coiled-coil domain undergoes an antiparallel interaction with a segment of the parallel coiled-coil dimer of Sas6.
source: By contrast, part of the Gorab monomer's coiled-coil domain undergoes an antiparallel interaction with a segment of the parallel coiled-coil dimer of Sas6.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data showing the orientation of the Gorab-Sas6 complex and HDX-MS data identifying interaction surfaces.

claim: The Gorab-Sas6 heterotrimeric complex can be visualized by electron microscopy.
source: This stable heterotrimeric complex can be visualized by electron microscopy.
evidence: This is directly supported by the rotary shadowing electron microscopy images presented in Figure 5.

claim: Mutation of leucine 447 in Sas6's Gorab-binding domain generates a Sas6 variant with a sixteenfold reduced binding affinity for Gorab.
source: Mutation of a single leucine residue in Sas6's Gorab-binding domain generates a Sas6 variant with a sixteenfold reduced binding affinity for Gorab that cannot support centriole duplication.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence correlation spectroscopy measurements showing KD values of 47 nM for wild-type and 798 nM for L447A mutant.

claim: Sas6 L447A cannot support centriole duplication.
source: Mutation of a single leucine residue in Sas6's Gorab-binding domain generates a Sas6 variant with a sixteenfold reduced binding affinity for Gorab that cannot support centriole duplication.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo data showing reduced centriole numbers and coordination defects in flies expressing Sas6-L447A.

claim: Gorab dimers at the Golgi exist in equilibrium with Sas6-associated monomers at the centriole.
source: Thus, Gorab dimers at the Golgi exist in equilibrium with Sas6-associated monomers at the centriole to balance Gorab's dual role.
evidence: This is supported by SEC-MALS data showing Gorab as a dimer alone and as a monomer in complex with Sas6, and by microscopy showing redistribution of Gorab upon Sas6 overexpression.

claim: The core components of centrioles and the molecules that regulate their assembly are highly conserved.
source: The core components of centrioles and the molecules that regulate their assembly are highly conserved (Brito et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Plk4 phosphorylates Ana2 at its N-terminal part, which promotes Ana2 recruitment to the site of procentriole formation.
source: Plk4 then phosphorylates Ana2 (Drosophila)/STIL(human) at its N-terminal part, which promotes Ana2 recruitment to the site of procentriole formation, and at its C-terminal part, which enables Ana2 to bind and thereby recruit Sas6 (Dzhindzhev et al., 2017; Dzhindzhev et al., 2014; McLamarrah et al., 2018; Ohta et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Plk4 phosphorylates Ana2 at its C-terminal part, which enables Ana2 to bind and thereby recruit Sas6.
source: Plk4 then phosphorylates Ana2 (Drosophila)/STIL(human) at its N-terminal part, which promotes Ana2 recruitment to the site of procentriole formation, and at its C-terminal part, which enables Ana2 to bind and thereby recruit Sas6 (Dzhindzhev et al., 2017; Dzhindzhev et al., 2014; McLamarrah et al., 2018; Ohta et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The assembly of a ninefold symmetrical arrangement of Sas6 dimers provides the structural basis for the ninefold symmetrical cartwheel structure at the procentriole's core.
source: The ensuing assembly of a ninefold symmetrical arrangement of Sas6 dimers provides the structural basis for the ninefold symmetrical cartwheel structure at the procentriole's core.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about centriole structure and Sas6 function.

claim: Sas6 interacts with Cep135 and in turn with Sas4/CPAP, which provides the linkage to centriole microtubules.
source: Sas6 interacts with Cep135 and in turn with Sas4 (Drosophila)/CPAP (human), which provides the linkage to centriole microtubules (Hiraki et al., 2007; Jerka-Dziadosz et al., 2010; Kohlmaier et al., 2009; Lin et al., 2013; Roque et al., 2012; Schmidt et al., 2009; Tang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Gorab is required to establish the ninefold symmetry of centrioles.
source: We recently identified an unexpected requirement for the protein, Gorab, to establish the ninefold symmetry of centrioles (Kovacs et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Flies lacking Gorab are uncoordinated due to basal body defects in sensory cilia, which lose their ninefold symmetry.
source: Flies lacking Gorab are uncoordinated due to basal body defects in sensory cilia, which lose their ninefold symmetry, and also exhibit maternal effect lethality due to failure of centriole duplication in the syncytial embryo.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (Kovacs et al., 2018).

claim: Flies lacking Gorab exhibit maternal effect lethality due to failure of centriole duplication in the syncytial embryo.
source: Flies lacking Gorab are uncoordinated due to basal body defects in sensory cilia, which lose their ninefold symmetry, and also exhibit maternal effect lethality due to failure of centriole duplication in the syncytial embryo.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work (Kovacs et al., 2018).

claim: Gorab is a trans-Golgi-associated protein.
source: Gorab is a trans-Golgi-associated protein.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data showing Gorab localization at the trans-Golgi.

claim: Human GORAB is mutated in the wrinkly skin disease, gerodermia osteodysplastica.
source: Its human counterpart is mutated in the wrinkly skin disease, gerodermia osteodysplastica (Burman et al., 2010; Burman et al., 2008; Di et al., 2003; Hennies et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A missense mutation in gerodermia patients disrupts the association of Gorab with the Golgi.
source: By copying a missense mutation in gerodermia patients that disrupts the association of Gorab with the Golgi, we were able to create mutant Drosophila Gorab also unable to localize to trans-Golgi.
evidence: This is supported by the authors' previous work (Kovacs et al., 2018) and data in the current manuscript.

claim: Mutant Drosophila Gorab unable to localize to trans-Golgi can still rescue the centriole and cilia defects of gorab null flies.
source: However, this mutant form of Gorab was still able to rescue the centriole and cilia defects of gorab null flies.
evidence: This is supported by the authors' previous work (Kovacs et al., 2018).

claim: Expression of C-terminally tagged Gorab disrupts Golgi functions in cytokinesis of male meiosis.
source: We also found that expression of C-terminally tagged Gorab disrupts Golgi functions in cytokinesis of male meiosis, a dominant phenotype that can be overcome by a second mutation preventing Golgi targeting (Hiraki et al., 2007; Lin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Centriole and Golgi functions of Drosophila Gorab are separable.
source: Thus, centriole and Golgi functions of Drosophila Gorab are separable.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Golgi-localization-deficient Gorab can still rescue centriole defects.

claim: Gorab resembles a group of homodimeric rod-like proteins, the golgins, which function in vesicle tethering.
source: Gorab resembles a group of homodimeric rod-like proteins, the golgins, which function in vesicle tethering (Short et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The golgins associate through their C-termini with different Golgi domains.
source: The golgins associate through their C-termini with different Golgi domains, and their N-termini both capture vesicles and provide specificity to their tethering (Gillingham and Munro, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The N-termini of golgins both capture vesicles and provide specificity to their tethering.
source: The golgins associate through their C-termini with different Golgi domains, and their N-termini both capture vesicles and provide specificity to their tethering (Gillingham and Munro, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: There is known redundancy of golgin function, reflected by the overlapping specificity of the types of vesicles they capture.
source: There is known redundancy of golgin function, reflected by the overlapping specificity of the types of vesicles they capture (Wong and Munro, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Gorab is rapidly displaced from the trans-side of the Golgi apparatus by Brefeldin A.
source: Gorab is rapidly displaced from the trans-side of the Golgi apparatus by Brefeldin A, suggesting that its peripheral membrane association requires ARF-GTPase activity (Egerer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Gorab's peripheral membrane association requires ARF-GTPase activity.
source: Gorab is rapidly displaced from the trans-side of the Golgi apparatus by Brefeldin A, suggesting that its peripheral membrane association requires ARF-GTPase activity (Egerer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is inferred from the Brefeldin A sensitivity and supported by a citation.

claim: Human Gorab can form a homodimer in complex with Rab6.
source: Previous studies of human Gorab indicated its ability to form a homodimer in complex with Rab6 and identified its putative coiled-coil region as a requirement to localize at the trans-Golgi (Egerer et al., 2015; Witkos et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The putative coiled-coil region of human Gorab is required to localize at the trans-Golgi.
source: Previous studies of human Gorab indicated its ability to form a homodimer in complex with Rab6 and identified its putative coiled-coil region as a requirement to localize at the trans-Golgi (Egerer et al., 2015; Witkos et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Drosophila Gorab can interact with itself, potentially through the predicted coiled-coil motif.
source: Our own studies on its Drosophila counterpart supported Gorab's ability to interact with itself, potentially through the predicted coiled-coil motif.
evidence: This is supported by the authors' previous work (Kovacs et al., 2018).

claim: The region of Gorab required for homodimerization overlaps with the region required for Gorab's interaction with Sas6.
source: However, we also found this region to overlap with the region required for Gorab's interaction with Sas6 (Kovacs et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by the authors' previous work (Kovacs et al., 2018).

claim: The theoretical mass of monomeric MBP-Gorab is 79.4 kDa.
source: Whereas the theoretical mass of monomeric MBP-Gorab is 79.4 kDa, SEC-MALS indicated the Mw of the protein eluting in the major peak as 146.1 kDa.
evidence: This is a calculated theoretical value based on the protein sequence.

claim: SEC-MALS indicates the molecular weight of MBP-Gorab eluting in the major peak as 146.1 kDa.
source: Whereas the theoretical mass of monomeric MBP-Gorab is 79.4 kDa, SEC-MALS indicated the Mw of the protein eluting in the major peak as 146.1 kDa.
evidence: This is directly measured by SEC-MALS as shown in Figure 1A.

claim: MBP-Gorab behaves as a dimer in solution.
source: Thus, similar to other golgins, MBP-Gorab behaves as a dimer in solution.
evidence: This is inferred from the SEC-MALS data showing a molecular weight approximately twice that of the monomer.

claim: The N-terminal part of Gorab (aa 1-200) is highly flexible.
source: The HDX pattern of Gorab after 10 s incubation with D2O buffer indicated almost complete exchange of hydrogen with deuterium in the N-terminal (aa 1–200) and very C-terminal parts (aa 318–338) of the protein, indicating high flexibility (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by HDX-MS data showing rapid deuterium exchange in this region, as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The very C-terminal part of Gorab (aa 318-338) is highly flexible.
source: The HDX pattern of Gorab after 10 s incubation with D2O buffer indicated almost complete exchange of hydrogen with deuterium in the N-terminal (aa 1–200) and very C-terminal parts (aa 318–338) of the protein, indicating high flexibility (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by HDX-MS data showing rapid deuterium exchange in this region, as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Restricted deuterium exchange in the C-terminal part of Gorab suggests three distinct protected, structured regions (aa 200-220, 230-240, and 252-315).
source: Restricted deuterium exchange in the C-terminal part suggested three distinct protected, structured regions (aa 200–220, 230–240, and 252–315) matching the coiled-coil predictions by the COILS program (Lupas et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 1B and comparison with COILS predictions.

claim: The protected regions in Gorab's C-terminal part match the coiled-coil predictions by the COILS program.
source: Restricted deuterium exchange in the C-terminal part suggested three distinct protected, structured regions (aa 200–220, 230–240, and 252–315) matching the coiled-coil predictions by the COILS program (Lupas et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of HDX-MS data with computational predictions.

claim: The dimerization of Gorab is driven by coiled-coil interactions on its C-terminus.
source: This suggests that the dimerization of Gorab might be driven by coiled-coil interactions on its C-terminus (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is inferred from the HDX-MS data showing protected regions matching coiled-coil predictions.

claim: After 150 min of HDX incubation, only the region between aa 270-287 of Gorab remained protected from deuterium exchange.
source: In the HDX experiment, longer periods of incubation identified regions permitting 'breathing' of this secondary structure (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), such that after 150 min only the region between aa 270–287, and especially aa 278–284, remained protected from the deuterium exchange.
evidence: This is directly shown by HDX-MS data in Figure 1C.

claim: The region aa 278-284 of Gorab shows the highest protection from deuterium exchange after 150 min.
source: In the HDX experiment, longer periods of incubation identified regions permitting 'breathing' of this secondary structure (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), such that after 150 min only the region between aa 270–287, and especially aa 278–284, remained protected from the deuterium exchange.
evidence: This is directly shown by HDX-MS data in Figure 1C.

claim: The high protection shown by region aa 278-284 of Gorab reflects regions of stability around the core of Gorab's dimerization domain.
source: The high protection shown by this region is most likely to reflect regions of stability around the core of Gorab's dimerization domain (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is inferred from the HDX-MS data showing persistent protection in this region.

claim: The aa 260-286 region of Gorab is essential for dimer formation.
source: This revealed that the aa 260–286 region is essential for dimer formation (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2) in accord with the findings of HDX-MS.
evidence: This is supported by SEC-MALS data of deletion constructs shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Deletions within other parts of the C-terminal domain of Gorab disrupt the dimeric structure and result in the formation of higher-order structures or mixtures with monomers.
source: Moreover, SEC-MALS data revealed that deletions within other parts of the C-terminal domain disrupt the dimeric structure of MBP-Gorab and result in the formation of higher-order structures, or mixtures of these with monomers (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by SEC-MALS data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The entire C-terminal domain (aa 200-320) of Gorab is organized to permit dimerization.
source: This suggests that the entire C-terminal domain (aa 200–320) is organized in such a way to permit dimerization and that even minor changes within the sequence lead to structural instability.
evidence: This is inferred from the SEC-MALS data showing that various deletions disrupt proper dimerization.

claim: Minor changes within the C-terminal domain sequence of Gorab lead to structural instability.
source: This suggests that the entire C-terminal domain (aa 200–320) is organized in such a way to permit dimerization and that even minor changes within the sequence lead to structural instability.
evidence: This is inferred from the SEC-MALS data showing that various deletions disrupt proper dimerization.

claim: Full-length eGFP-Gorab localizes in the position of the trans-Golgi in large primary spermatocytes.
source: In agreement with our earlier findings (Kovacs et al., 2018), the vast majority of wild-type eGFP-Gorab localized in the position of the trans-Golgi, inside the Golgi cisternae and surrounded by the GM130 cis-Golgi marker, in large primary spermatocytes (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The majority of full-length eGFP-Gorab colocalizes with Golgin-245 trans-Golgi marker in primary spermatocytes and wing imaginal discs.
source: Accordingly, the majority of FL eGFP-Gorab colocalized with Golgin-245 trans-Golgi marker as we observed in primary spermatocytes and wing imaginal discs and, in accord with our previous findings, a small fraction of FL Gorab was recruited to centrosomes (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: A small fraction of full-length Gorab is recruited to centrosomes.
source: Accordingly, the majority of FL eGFP-Gorab colocalized with Golgin-245 trans-Golgi marker as we observed in primary spermatocytes and wing imaginal discs and, in accord with our previous findings, a small fraction of FL Gorab was recruited to centrosomes (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Gorab Δ282-286 does not localize to the Golgi but retains its centrosomal localization.
source: By contrast, Gorab Δ282–286 did not localize to the Golgi but retained its centrosomal localization both in primary spermatocytes and in wing disc cells (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Ubq-Gorab Δ282-286 fully rescues the coordination, viability, and fertility defects of gorab mutants.
source: In line with its centriolar localization, Ubq-Gorab Δ282–286 was able to fully rescue the coordination, viability, and fertility defects of gorab mutants (Kovacs et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by phenotypic rescue data and a citation to previous work.

claim: Dimerization of Gorab is required for its trans-Golgi localization but not for its centriolar localization and function.
source: This indicates that dimerization of Gorab is required for its trans-Golgi localization but not for its centriolar localization and function.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the dimerization-deficient Δ282-286 mutant localizes to centrioles and rescues gorab mutant phenotypes but does not localize to the Golgi.

claim: When mixed in a molar ratio 1 part Gorab : 2 parts Sas6, a stable complex is formed.
source: SEC confirmed that when mixed in a molar ratio 1 part Gorab : 2 parts Sas6, a stable complex was formed (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by SEC data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The molecular mass of the Gorab-Sas6 complex is 258.7 kDa.
source: MALS measurements indicated the molecular mass of this complex eluting in the major peak to be 258.7 kDa (±0.061%), which would correspond to a heterotrimer of homodimeric MBP-Sas6 and monomeric MBP-Gorab, whose theoretical mass is 272.2 kDa (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is directly measured by SEC-MALS as shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The Gorab-Sas6 complex corresponds to a heterotrimer of homodimeric MBP-Sas6 and monomeric MBP-Gorab.
source: MALS measurements indicated the molecular mass of this complex eluting in the major peak to be 258.7 kDa (±0.061%), which would correspond to a heterotrimer of homodimeric MBP-Sas6 and monomeric MBP-Gorab, whose theoretical mass is 272.2 kDa (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is inferred from the measured molecular mass being consistent with the theoretical mass of a 2:1 Sas6:Gorab complex.

claim: Gorab is a dimer in solution but binds Sas6 dimer as a monomer.
source: This indicates that Gorab is a dimer in solution but binds Sas6 dimer as a monomer.
evidence: This is inferred from SEC-MALS data showing Gorab as a dimer alone and as a monomer in the Sas6 complex.

claim: The 230-260 aa segment of Gorab becomes more stable when Gorab is in complex with Sas6.
source: The 230–260 aa segment became slightly more stable when Gorab was in complex with Sas6 than when on its own (Figure 2C, pink box, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The 270-315 aa segment of Gorab becomes destabilized when Gorab is in complex with Sas6.
source: In contrast, the 270–315 aa segment appeared to be destabilized (Figure 2c, blue box, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The 230-260 aa segment of Gorab represents the interaction surface between Gorab and Sas6.
source: It is most likely that the 230–260 aa segment of Gorab, which is stabilized upon Sas6 binding, represents the interaction surface between the two proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the HDX-MS data showing stabilization of this region upon complex formation.

claim: The aa 270-315 segment at the dimerization core of Gorab becomes destabilized when Gorab dissociates to a monomer during complex formation with Sas6.
source: As Gorab appears to dissociate to a monomer during complex formation with Sas6, this suggests that the aa 270–315 segment at the dimerization core (Figure 1C, D) becomes destabilized.
evidence: This is inferred from the HDX-MS data showing destabilization of the dimerization core region when Gorab binds Sas6.

claim: Gorab Δ244-259 aa is the shortest deletion that gives the maximal observed decrease in Sas6 binding.
source: This revealed Gorab Δ244–259 aa as the shortest deletion that gives the maximal observed decrease in Sas6 binding.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assays shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The 244-260 aa region of Gorab binds strongly to Sas6.
source: These findings accord with the HDX data and strongly suggest that the 244–260 aa region of Gorab binds strongly to Sas6 and that weaker interacting surfaces extend between aa 219–244 and aa 260–270 (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: This is supported by deletion analysis and HDX-MS data.

claim: Weaker Gorab-Sas6 interacting surfaces extend between aa 219-244 and aa 260-270 of Gorab.
source: These findings accord with the HDX data and strongly suggest that the 244–260 aa region of Gorab binds strongly to Sas6 and that weaker interacting surfaces extend between aa 219–244 and aa 260–270 (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: This is supported by deletion analysis showing partial binding with flanking deletions.

claim: The Sas6 region aa 440-460 shows increased stability when in complex with Gorab.
source: We observed clear differences in deuteration level within 20 residues (aa 440–460) towards the C-terminus of Sas6 that showed increased stability when in complex with Gorab (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The Sas6 region aa 351-472 is sufficient to bind Gorab.
source: However, our previous study showed that the Sas6 region aa 351–472 (Kovacs et al., 2018) is sufficient to bind Gorab.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The Sas6 segment aa 404-463 forms a stable complex with the 191-279 aa segment of Gorab.
source: Moreover, we found that the Sas6 segment aa 404–463 forms a stable complex with the 191–279 aa segment of Gorab (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by SEC-MALS data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The Sas6 region aa 440-460 lies on the interaction surface with Gorab.
source: We therefore concluded that the Sas6 region aa 440–460, showing the highest protection from HDX upon Gorab binding, lies on the interaction surface.
evidence: This is inferred from the HDX-MS data showing protection in this region upon Gorab binding.

claim: Sas6 L447A is not able to bind Gorab in vitro.
source: These experiments indicated that Sas6 L447A was not able to bind Gorab in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assays and SEC data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The KD of Gorab's interaction with wild-type Sas6 is 47 nM.
source: Our measurements revealed that the KD of Gorab's interaction with wild-type Sas6 was in the low nanomolar range of 47 nM, but that the binding strength to Sas6 L447A mutant was 16 times weaker (KD = 798 nM).
evidence: This is directly measured by fluorescence correlation spectroscopy as shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The binding strength of Gorab to Sas6 L447A mutant is 16 times weaker than to wild-type Sas6.
source: Our measurements revealed that the KD of Gorab's interaction with wild-type Sas6 was in the low nanomolar range of 47 nM, but that the binding strength to Sas6 L447A mutant was 16 times weaker (KD = 798 nM).
evidence: This is calculated from the FCS measurements showing KD values of 47 nM and 798 nM.

claim: The KD of Gorab's interaction with Sas6 L447A is 798 nM.
source: Our measurements revealed that the KD of Gorab's interaction with wild-type Sas6 was in the low nanomolar range of 47 nM, but that the binding strength to Sas6 L447A mutant was 16 times weaker (KD = 798 nM).
evidence: This is directly measured by fluorescence correlation spectroscopy as shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Sas6-wild type, Sas6-M440A, Sas6-L447A, Sas6-S452A, and Sas6-L456A all display the same elution profile in SEC.
source: We found that Sas6-wild type, Sas6-M440A, Sas6-L447A, Sas6-S452A, and Sas6-L456A all displayed the same elution profile in SEC (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is supported by SEC data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: All of the Sas6 point mutants (M440A, L447A, S452A, L456A) are able to form homodimers.
source: This indicates that all of the Sas6 point mutants behave like Sas6-wild type in being able to form homodimers.
evidence: This is inferred from the SEC data showing similar elution profiles for all mutants.

claim: L447 is located at position 'a' of the 'a-g' heptad repeats in the Sas6 coiled coil.
source: Moreover, L447, which is located at the C-terminal region of the coiled coil of Sas6, is predicted to lie at position 'a' of the 'a-g' heptad repeats with M440 lying in a similar position (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A, B).
evidence: This is based on computational prediction shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: M440 lies at position 'a' of the 'a-g' heptad repeats in the Sas6 coiled coil.
source: Moreover, L447, which is located at the C-terminal region of the coiled coil of Sas6, is predicted to lie at position 'a' of the 'a-g' heptad repeats with M440 lying in a similar position (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A, B).
evidence: This is based on computational prediction shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Sas6-M440A has a BUDE energy of -717.
source: Our modeling analysis using CCBuilder 2.0 (Wood and Woolfson, 2018) predicts that mutants M440A and L447A have a BUDE energy of –717 and –714, respectively, which is very similar to that of Sas6-wild type (−724) (Figure 3—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is based on computational modeling using CCBuilder 2.0.

claim: Sas6-L447A has a BUDE energy of -714.
source: Our modeling analysis using CCBuilder 2.0 (Wood and Woolfson, 2018) predicts that mutants M440A and L447A have a BUDE energy of –717 and –714, respectively, which is very similar to that of Sas6-wild type (−724) (Figure 3—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is based on computational modeling using CCBuilder 2.0.

claim: Sas6-wild type has a BUDE energy of -724.
source: Our modeling analysis using CCBuilder 2.0 (Wood and Woolfson, 2018) predicts that mutants M440A and L447A have a BUDE energy of –717 and –714, respectively, which is very similar to that of Sas6-wild type (−724) (Figure 3—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is based on computational modeling using CCBuilder 2.0.

claim: The L447A mutation does not prevent Sas6 from forming a homodimer.
source: We therefore conclude that the L447A does not prevent Sas6 from forming a homodimer but the local structure around L447 might be partially perturbed in the mutant L447A.
evidence: This is inferred from the SEC data showing similar elution profiles and the BUDE energy calculations.

claim: The local structure around L447 might be partially perturbed in the mutant Sas6-L447A.
source: We therefore conclude that the L447A does not prevent Sas6 from forming a homodimer but the local structure around L447 might be partially perturbed in the mutant L447A.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that L447A prevents Gorab binding despite maintaining dimer formation.

claim: Subtle changes in the local region around L447 are sufficient to prevent the interaction of Sas6-L447A with Gorab.
source: Such subtle change in the local region seems to be sufficient to prevent the interaction of Sas6-L447A with Gorab.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that L447A maintains dimer formation but loses Gorab binding.

claim: Expression of wild-type Sas6 completely rescues the eclosion phenotype of the sas6 null mutant.
source: These mutant phenotypes were completely rescued by the elevated expression of wild-type or M440A Sas6 transgenes (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is supported by eclosion assay data shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: Expression of Sas6-M440A completely rescues the eclosion phenotype of the sas6 null mutant.
source: These mutant phenotypes were completely rescued by the elevated expression of wild-type or M440A Sas6 transgenes (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is supported by eclosion assay data shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: Sas6 L447A is able to rescue the eclosion phenotype of the sas6 null mutant.
source: In contrast, Sas6 L447A was able to rescue the eclosion phenotype of the sas6 null and could only partially the coordination phenotype such that 30% of these flies were able to pass the climbing test (Figure 3D–F, Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by eclosion assay data shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: Sas6 L447A can only partially rescue the coordination phenotype of the sas6 null mutant, with 30% of flies able to pass the climbing test.
source: In contrast, Sas6 L447A was able to rescue the eclosion phenotype of the sas6 null and could only partially the coordination phenotype such that 30% of these flies were able to pass the climbing test (Figure 3D–F, Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by climbing assay data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: At 29°C, both gorab1 and gorab2 mutant alleles display similarly severe uncoordination defects.
source: When gorab1 and gorab2 flies are raised at 29°C, both mutant alleles display similarly severe uncoordination defects and the flies are completely unable to climb.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experiments.

claim: At 25°C, gorab2 flies show severe total loss of coordination.
source: At 25°C, however, gorab2 flies showed a similarly severe total loss of coordination, whereas gorab1 flies were moderately uncoordinated with around 25% being able to climb 5 cm in 15 s (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by climbing assay data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: At 25°C, gorab1 flies are moderately uncoordinated with around 25% being able to climb 5 cm in 15 s.
source: At 25°C, however, gorab2 flies showed a similarly severe total loss of coordination, whereas gorab1 flies were moderately uncoordinated with around 25% being able to climb 5 cm in 15 s (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by climbing assay data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The extent of rescue of the coordination phenotype of the sas6 null by overexpression of Sas6 L447A is reminiscent of the gorab1 hypomorph.
source: Thus the extent of rescue of the coordination phenotype of the sas6 null by overexpression of Sas6 L447A was reminiscent of the gorab1 hypomorph (Figure 3F, Videos 1 and 2) and in accord with the greatly reduced ability of Sas6-L447A to bind Gorab.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the climbing assay results of Sas6-L447A rescue with gorab1 mutant phenotype.

claim: Expression of wild-type Sas6 fully rescues the centriole loss of sas6 null larvae in interphase cells.
source: We found that the elevated expression of both wild-type Sas6 and the Sas6-M440A transgene from the Act5C-GAL4 driver fully rescued the centriole loss of sas6 null larvae in interphase cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by centriole counting data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of Sas6-M440A fully rescues the centriole loss of sas6 null larvae in interphase cells.
source: We found that the elevated expression of both wild-type Sas6 and the Sas6-M440A transgene from the Act5C-GAL4 driver fully rescued the centriole loss of sas6 null larvae in interphase cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by centriole counting data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sas6 L447A gives only partial rescue, restoring only 8% of centriole numbers in interphase cells.
source: By contrast, Sas6 L447A gave only partial rescue restoring only 8% of centriole numbers.
evidence: This is supported by centriole counting data.

claim: In the gorab2 null mutant, centrosomes are absent.
source: This compares to the gorab2 null mutant in which centrosomes are absent and the gorab1 hypomorph, in which centrosome numbers are reduced to around 35% of wild type.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experiments.

claim: In the gorab1 hypomorph, centrosome numbers are reduced to around 35% of wild type.
source: This compares to the gorab2 null mutant in which centrosomes are absent and the gorab1 hypomorph, in which centrosome numbers are reduced to around 35% of wild type.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experiments.

claim: Expression of wild-type Sas6 totally rescues the complete mitotic centrosome loss of the sas6 null.
source: Whereas expression of wild-type Sas6 or Sas6-M440A totally rescued the complete mitotic centrosome loss of the sas6 null, expression of Sas6-L477A resulted in partial rescue in which we observed several phenotypic categories (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is supported by mitotic centriole analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Expression of Sas6-M440A totally rescues the complete mitotic centrosome loss of the sas6 null.
source: Whereas expression of wild-type Sas6 or Sas6-M440A totally rescued the complete mitotic centrosome loss of the sas6 null, expression of Sas6-L477A resulted in partial rescue in which we observed several phenotypic categories (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is supported by mitotic centriole analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Expression of Sas6-L447A in the sas6 null background results in a phenotype most similar to that of heteroallelic gorab1/gorab2 flies or gorab2 null flies.
source: The distribution of cells exhibiting these phenotypes indicated that expression of Sas6 L447A in the sas6 null background resulted in a phenotype most similar to that of heteroallelic gorab1/gorab2 flies or gorab2 null flies.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the distribution of phenotypic categories across genotypes shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The consequences of Sas6-L447A upon centrosome number accord with the protein having reduced ability to bind Gorab.
source: Thus, the consequences of Sas6-L447A upon centrosome number accord with the protein having reduced ability to bind Gorab.
evidence: This is inferred from the similarity between Sas6-L447A phenotype and gorab mutant phenotypes.

claim: Sas6-M440A is still able to recruit Gorab to the centrosome in vivo.
source: If the above interpretation is correct, then Sas6-M440A should still able to recruit Gorab to the centrosome in vivo, whereas Sas6-L447A should not.
evidence: This is predicted based on the binding data and confirmed by microscopy in Figure 4C.

claim: Gorab can be detected on centrosomes rescued by wild-type Sas6 or Sas6-M440A.
source: Asl staining revealed centrosomes to be absent in sas6 null discs and rescued by either wild-type Sas6 or Sas6-M440A in both interphase and mitotic cells (Figure 4C). In all cases, Gorab could be detected on these rescued centrosomes.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Gorab cannot be detected on the rare centrosomes present following expression of Sas6-L447A in the sas6 null background.
source: We were, however, unable to detect Gorab on the rare centrosomes present following expression of Sas6-L447A in the sas6 null background irrespective of the intensity of Asl or Rcd4 staining (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, n = 243 centrioles counted in total).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data examining 243 centrioles.

claim: Sas6-L447A is still able to localize to the centrioles.
source: Thus, Sas6-L447A binds Gorab extremely poorly in vitro and is unable to recruit Gorab onto the centriole in vivo, a property that is associated with dramatically reduced centriole duplication even though Sas6 L447A is still able to localize to the centrioles (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The L447-dependent interaction of Sas6 with Gorab mediates Gorab's association with the centrosome.
source: Together, these results show that the L447-dependent interaction of Sas6 with Gorab mediates Gorab's association with the centrosome, and as a consequence, the phenotype of Sas6-L447A strongly resembles that of a gorab strong hypomorph.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing that L447A prevents Gorab recruitment and phenocopies gorab mutants.

claim: The phenotype of Sas6-L447A strongly resembles that of a gorab strong hypomorph.
source: Together, these results show that the L447-dependent interaction of Sas6 with Gorab mediates Gorab's association with the centrosome, and as a consequence, the phenotype of Sas6-L447A strongly resembles that of a gorab strong hypomorph.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of phenotypic data between Sas6-L447A and gorab mutants.

claim: Sas6 exists as a parallel dimer in which the two globular head domains lie on one end of a coiled coil of mean length 41 nm.
source: The appearance of Sas6 FL molecules confirms previous findings (Cottee et al., 2015; Kitagawa et al., 2011; Qiao et al., 2012; van Breugel et al., 2011) that Sas6 exists as a parallel dimer in which the two globular head domains lie on one end of a coiled coil, visible as a long rod of mean length 41 nm (n = 106) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5B and citations to previous studies.

claim: When Sas6 FL is complexed to MBP-Gorab FL, the two globular head domains of Sas6 and one globular domain of MBP are separated by a long coiled-coil rod.
source: When Sas6 FL was complexed to the different constructs of N-terminally MBP-tagged Gorab, we observed the two globular head domains of Sas6 and one globular domain of MBP to be separated by a long coiled-coil rod (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5C-E.

claim: The mean length of the rod between the Sas6 head domains and the MBP tag in the Sas6-MBP-Gorab FL complex is 54.8 nm.
source: The mean length of the rod between the Sas6 head domains and the MBP tag was greater than the Sas6's coiled-coil rod alone; 54.8 nm (n = 87), 51.5 nm (n = 118), and 49.6 nm (n = 114) for Sas6 in complex with MBP-Gorab FL, MBP-Gorab CC long, and MBP-Gorab CC short, respectively (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is measured from electron microscopy images and quantified in Figure 5F.

claim: The mean length of the rod between the Sas6 head domains and the MBP tag in the Sas6-MBP-Gorab CC long complex is 51.5 nm.
source: The mean length of the rod between the Sas6 head domains and the MBP tag was greater than the Sas6's coiled-coil rod alone; 54.8 nm (n = 87), 51.5 nm (n = 118), and 49.6 nm (n = 114) for Sas6 in complex with MBP-Gorab FL, MBP-Gorab CC long, and MBP-Gorab CC short, respectively (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is measured from electron microscopy images and quantified in Figure 5F.

claim: The mean length of the rod between the Sas6 head domains and the MBP tag in the Sas6-MBP-Gorab CC short complex is 49.6 nm.
source: The mean length of the rod between the Sas6 head domains and the MBP tag was greater than the Sas6's coiled-coil rod alone; 54.8 nm (n = 87), 51.5 nm (n = 118), and 49.6 nm (n = 114) for Sas6 in complex with MBP-Gorab FL, MBP-Gorab CC long, and MBP-Gorab CC short, respectively (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is measured from electron microscopy images and quantified in Figure 5F.

claim: Sas6 forms a parallel dimer and a Gorab monomer binds Sas6 dimer in an antiparallel manner.
source: These observations confirm that Sas6 forms a parallel dimer and indicate that a Gorab monomer binds Sas6 dimer in an antiparallel manner.
evidence: This is inferred from the electron microscopy data showing the arrangement of the complex.

claim: The C-terminal region of Gorab (aa 223-338) is able to weakly bind Rab6.
source: This revealed that C-terminal region of Gorab (aa 223–338) is able to weakly bind Rab6.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assays shown in Figure 6B.

claim: For a complete interaction with Rab6, a longer C-terminal region of Gorab (195-338 aa) is needed.
source: However, for a complete interaction with Rab6, a longer C-terminal region of Gorab (195–338 aa) is needed (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assays shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The ability for Gorab to form a dimer is critical for complex formation between Gorab and Rab6.
source: Thus, the ability for Gorab to form a dimer appears critical for complex formation between Gorab and Rab6.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the Rab6-binding region encompasses the dimerization domain.

claim: The C-terminal 'half' of Gorab (aa 195-338) is sufficient for Golgi localization.
source: We were, however, able to show that the C-terminal Rab6-binding domain of Gorab was sufficient for its Golgi localization by expressing the GFP-tagged C-terminal domain (aa 195–338) alone in flies and demonstrating that it could localize adjacent to GM130 at the Golgi and alongside dPLP at the centriole (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Gorab does not localize to the Golgi in rab6-/- cells.
source: Whereas Gorab localized to the Golgi alongside GM130 in rab6+/- cells, cells from the rab6-/- clone had no Gorab at the Golgi (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data of rab6 mutant clones shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Interactions between the dimerizing C-terminal part of Gorab and Rab6 are required for Gorab to localize to the Golgi.
source: Together, this strongly suggests that interactions between the dimerizing C-terminal part of Gorab and Rab6 are required for Gorab to localize to the Golgi.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing that the C-terminal domain binds Rab6, is sufficient for Golgi localization, and Gorab fails to localize to Golgi in rab6 mutants.

claim: Rab6 binds Gorab only as a dimer.
source: We showed that Rab6 binds Gorab only as a dimer, but is not able to interact with Gorab when in complex with Sas6 (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assays shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Rab6 is not able to interact with Gorab when Gorab is in complex with Sas6.
source: We showed that Rab6 binds Gorab only as a dimer, but is not able to interact with Gorab when in complex with Sas6 (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro binding assays shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Gorab's interaction with Sas6 is much stronger than its interaction with Rab6.
source: This result strongly suggests that the Gorab's interaction with Sas6 is much stronger than its interaction with Rab6.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Rab6 cannot bind Gorab when Gorab is complexed with Sas6, and confirmed by ITC measurements.

claim: The Gorab-Rab6 complex has a KD of 2.24 µM.
source: We were able to confirm this using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), which revealed that the Gorab–Rab6 complex showed a KD of 2.24 µM.
evidence: This is directly measured by ITC as shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The interaction between Gorab and Rab6 is significantly weaker than that between Gorab and Sas6.
source: Thus, the interaction between Gorab and Rab6 is significantly weaker than that between Gorab and Sas6 (KD = 47 nM) (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the KD values measured by ITC and FCS.

claim: Increased expression of Sas6 leads to a reduction in the amount of Gorab associating with the Golgi apparatus.
source: A stronger interaction of Gorab with Sas6 than with itself and Rab6 leads to the prediction that increased expression of Sas6 should lead to a reduction in the amount of Gorab associating with the Golgi apparatus. Indeed, we were able to see this in the experiments described above (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is predicted based on the relative binding affinities and confirmed by microscopy data in Figure 4B.

claim: Elevated expression of wild-type Sas6 increases the GFP-Gorab signal intensity at the centrosomes and reduces it at the Golgi.
source: The elevated expression of both wild-type Sas6 and Sas6-M440A in a sas6 background had the effect of increasing the GFP-Gorab signal intensity at the centrosomes and reducing it at the Golgi.
evidence: This is observed in the microscopy data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Elevated expression of Sas6-M440A increases the GFP-Gorab signal intensity at the centrosomes and reduces it at the Golgi.
source: The elevated expression of both wild-type Sas6 and Sas6-M440A in a sas6 background had the effect of increasing the GFP-Gorab signal intensity at the centrosomes and reducing it at the Golgi.
evidence: This is observed in the microscopy data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Elevated expression of Sas6-L447A does not affect the Golgi pool of Gorab.
source: By contrast, elevated expression Sas6-L447A in the sas6 null background did not affect the Golgi pool of Gorab, which was not recruited to residual centrosomes, that could have robust staining of Asl (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is observed in the microscopy data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The relative levels of Gorab at the centriole and Golgi are set by its high affinity to Sas6 and the concentration of Sas6 at the centriole.
source: Thus, it seems that the relative levels of Gorab at the centriole and Golgi are set by its high affinity to Sas6 and the concentration of Sas6 at the centriole.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Sas6 overexpression redistributes Gorab from Golgi to centrioles.

claim: Gorab exists at the trans-Golgi network as a homodimer.
source: Together, our findings indicate that Gorab exists at the trans-Golgi network as a homodimer.
evidence: This is supported by SEC-MALS data and the requirement for dimerization for Golgi localization.

claim: Gorab dimerization requires its coiled-coil motif (residues 200-315).
source: Dimerization requires its coiled-coil motif (residues 200–315) within which is a core sequence (residues 270–287) that represents the most stable part of this dimerization region.
evidence: This is supported by HDX-MS and SEC-MALS data of deletion constructs.

claim: Residues 270-287 of Gorab represent the most stable part of the dimerization region.
source: Dimerization requires its coiled-coil motif (residues 200–315) within which is a core sequence (residues 270–287) that represents the most stable part of this dimerization region.
evidence: This is supported by HDX-MS data showing persistent protection in this region.

claim: Gorab dimerization enables Gorab to interact with Rab6.
source: Dimerization enables Gorab to interact with Rab6, and this in turn enables its association with the trans-Golgi.
evidence: This is supported by binding assays and the observation that dimerization-deficient Gorab does not localize to Golgi.

claim: Gorab's interaction with Rab6 enables its association with the trans-Golgi.
source: Dimerization enables Gorab to interact with Rab6, and this in turn enables its association with the trans-Golgi.
evidence: This is supported by the observation that Gorab does not localize to Golgi in rab6 mutants.

claim: Gorab interacts with Sas6 as a monomer.
source: In contrast, Gorab interacts with Sas6 as a monomer.
evidence: This is supported by SEC-MALS data showing the stoichiometry of the Gorab-Sas6 complex.

claim: Gorab's binding to Sas6 occurs with a higher affinity than its homodimerization.
source: Gorab's binding to Sas6 occurs with a higher affinity than its homodimerization, enabling a Gorab monomer to associate with the Sas6 dimer.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Gorab dissociates from a dimer to bind Sas6 and from the relative KD values.

claim: The relatively small number of Sas6 molecules at the centriole would more avidly bind the Gorab monomer, allowing greater excess of Gorab to accumulate as dimers at the trans-Golgi.
source: Thus, the relatively small number of Sas6 molecules at the centriole would more avidly bind the Gorab monomer, allowing greater excess of Gorab to accumulate as dimers at the trans-Golgi (Figure 7).
evidence: This is inferred from the relative binding affinities and the observed distribution of Gorab.

claim: Sas6 and Gorab interact through short interfaces within their coiled-coil regions.
source: Sas6 and Gorab interact through short interfaces within their coiled-coil regions.
evidence: This is supported by HDX-MS data identifying specific regions of interaction.

claim: Loss of human GORAB affects Golgi functions in just bone and skin when COPI function is required in multiple tissues.
source: However, its precise role in the transport of COPI vesicles is not clear, particularly why loss of human GORAB affects Golgi functions in just bone and skin when COPI function is required in multiple tissues.
evidence: This is stated as an unresolved question based on known tissue-specific phenotypes of GORAB mutations.

claim: The heterotrimeric structure formed by a Sas6 dimer and the Gorab monomer constitutes a single spoke plus central hub unit of the centriole's cartwheel.
source: The heterotrimeric structure formed by a Sas6 dimer and the Gorab monomer will together constitute a single spoke plus central hub unit of the centriole's cartwheel.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data and the known architecture of the centriole cartwheel.

claim: The C-terminal part of Gorab would be expected to lie in a tight antiparallel association with the C-terminal part of Sas6's coiled-coil region.
source: The C-terminal part of Gorab would be expected to lie in a tight antiparallel association with the C-terminal part of Sas6's coiled-coil region.
evidence: This is inferred from the electron microscopy data showing antiparallel orientation.

claim: Gorab's N-terminus might extend towards the centriolar microtubules and their associated proteins.
source: Gorab's N-terminus might thus be expected to extend towards the centriolar microtubules and their associated proteins (Figure 7).
evidence: This is speculated based on the orientation of Gorab in the Sas6 complex and the architecture of the centriole.

claim: Gorab might interact with the centriole wall in a region occupied in other cell types by the C-tubule.
source: As the microtubules of Drosophila's somatic centrioles exist as doublets of A- and B-tubules, it is tempting to speculate that Gorab interacts with the centriole wall in a region occupied in other cell types by the C-tubule.
evidence: This is speculated based on the structural arrangement and the observation that Gorab is not required in male germ-line centrioles with triplet microtubules.

claim: The lack of requirement for Sas6-Gorab interaction in the male germ-line could be explained by centrioles having triplet microtubules with a C-tubule occupying the space where Gorab would otherwise interact.
source: This could account for the lack of any requirement for Sas6–Gorab interaction in the male germ-line, where centrioles have triplet microtubules and a C-tubule occupies this space.
evidence: This is speculated to explain the tissue-specific requirement for Gorab.
